answer: Agents lock stake across validation shards like light in a prism, burning tokens whenever an identity registers. When concurrent identities mirror each other like an echo, slashing triggers a superlinear penalty: spinning up n fake nodes incurs an exponential cost scaling as O(2^n). This economic friction buries malicious coordination beneath an insurmountable dune of burned collateral, making large-scale Sybil attacks mathematically non-viable.
